# Languages and accuracy

<!-- Generated by dictionaries/pages.py from dictionaries/catalog, dictionaries/sources.json and dictionaries/policy.json; do not edit. -->

The v1.0.0 release has a dictionary package for 224 languages.
Accuracy is exact lemma match on the gold tokens of Universal Dependencies 2.19,
as scored by [`dictionaries/evaluate.py`](../dictionaries/evaluate.py). *Copy*
is the accuracy of returning every token unchanged.

| Scored on | Languages | Macro accuracy, % | Copy, % |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| test | 103 | 89.85 | 58.41 |
| 2-fold | 109 | 73.87 | 57.54 |
| — | 12 | — | — |

- **test**: the official test split. The dictionary learned from train; dev
  chose its options and then joined the final refit.
- **test†** (19 languages): as *test*, but the treebank has no dev split,
  so the options were chosen on a stand-in carved from the training split (see
  [Data use](../dictionaries/README.md#data-use)).
- **2-fold**: the treebank has no training split. It is cut into two halves (by
  document where the treebank marks documents, otherwise by sentence, so halves
  may share a document) and each half is scored by a build that learned from the
  other. The shipped package learned from the whole treebank. These treebanks
  are small, often a few hundred sentences, so the estimate is noisy.
- **—**: no gold lemmas. The package holds dictionary entries only; its accuracy
  is unmeasured.

For languages without an official dev split (test† and 2-fold), the dev
stand-in was introduced after the first test evaluation, so their scores are
partly exploratory.

Packages ending in `-nc` are for non-commercial use only; see
[DICTIONARY_LICENSES.md](../DICTIONARY_LICENSES.md). The build report, with the
dictionary order chosen on dev and the gate statistics, is
[`dictionaries/catalog/EVALUATION.md`](../dictionaries/catalog/EVALUATION.md).
